The review states that aldehyde/ketone chromophores can be converted to oximes with hydroxylamine hydrochloride before OXE formation. Scope: General OXE-route support; exact substrate scope still needs per-candidate route check.

The source describes one-step esterification of the generated oxime using base and an acid chloride. Scope: Directly supports OXE formation, but acid chloride identity and regioisomerism need candidate-level control.

The paper links OXE photoexcitation to N-O cleavage and radical generation, matching the Type-I validation lane. Scope: Mechanistic support; predicted candidates still require N-O BDE and excited-state checks.

Triphenylamine-based oxime ester access is described through arylamine formation by C-N coupling, followed by formylation, oximation and condensation. Scope: Supports donor installation in OXE-like routes; catalyst/ligand scope must be checked for each aryl halide.

The quinoxalinoid chromophore synthesis uses Sonogashira chemistry to access a diarylacetylene precursor. Scope: Strong support for ethynyl-extended chromophores; not automatically proof of PI activity.

A two-photon polymerization photoinitiator library of expanded alpha,beta-unsaturated ketones was prepared using Sonogashira and condensation steps. Scope: Supports ethynyl bridge construction in high-2PA PI-like chromophores; reaction conditions remain substrate-specific.

The source describes aldehyde-cycloketone condensation to make donor-substituted alpha,beta-unsaturated ketone photoinitiator scaffolds. Scope: The paper names aldol condensation rather than Knoevenagel; use as Knoevenagel/aldol-family support.
Carbazole donor hemicyanine 2PA chromophores were prepared by Knoevenagel condensation. Scope: Supports donor-acceptor chromophore formation; PI initiating-center closure must be added separately.

ITX photoinitiator derivatives were diversified by Suzuki coupling, supporting donor/aryl expansion of benchmark PI scaffolds. Scope: Good route support for donor-tuned benchmark lanes; still requires 2PA and initiation mechanism checks.

The paper explicitly assembles potential donor-acceptor-donor two-photon photoinitiators by Suzuki cross-coupling. Scope: Strongest support for Suzuki-based D-A-D PI enumeration; generated products still need strict PI role closure.

The quinoxalinoid chromophore route installs amine donors through sequential Buchwald-Hartwig amination steps. Scope: Supports donor installation in complex chromophores; PI initiating center is not inherent in this source.

The quinoxaline 2PA chromophore synthesis uses Heck coupling for key intermediates and target chromophores, supporting styryl-extension templates. Scope: Direct for high-2PA chromophore construction; PI function must come from the chosen initiating center.

The paper assigns triphenylamine as donor, triazine as acceptor and styryl as chromophore in D-pi-A triazine systems. Scope: Supports the triazine D-pi-A design motif, not a direct nucleophilic triazine substitution protocol in this local PDF.

The source uses a trichloromethyl-triazine sensitizer/initiator system, supporting triazine as a productive PI motif under the right chemistry. Scope: This is mechanism/motif support, not direct support for donor substitution enumeration.

The paper describes acylphosphine oxide synthesis from an acid chloride and phosphine reagent through Michaelis-Arbuzov chemistry. Scope: Route support is strong, but APO candidates remain benchmark/watchlist unless donor-rich 2PA role closure is achieved.

The review identifies TPO and BAPO as widely used Type-I photoinitiators, supporting an APO benchmark lane. Scope: Benchmark support only; APO derivatives should not compete directly with OXE mainline without 2PA closure.

The source constructs quinoxaline-related carbonyl intermediates by Friedel-Crafts acylation, supporting aryl-acylation logic. Scope: Analogous carbonyl-building support, not a universal benzophenone acylation recipe.

The review anchors benzophenone and thioxanthone carbonyls as Type-II PI centers with hydrogen-abstraction logic. Scope: Mechanism support; coinitiator dependence and intramolecular H-donor availability must be tracked.

The review supports the Type-II lane by linking benzophenone/thioxanthone-like systems to H-abstraction or ET with coinitiators. Scope: Mechanistic support is coinitiator-aware; single-component PI claims need extra validation.
